title: Complete the Sudoku Board (Backtracking + Constraints)
real_world_story: A Sudoku app receives a partially filled 9x9 board with dots for empty cells. The hint engine must fill every empty cell so each row, column, and 3x3 box contains digits 1-9 exactly once.

real_world_connection.input_represents: 9x9 board where '.' is an empty cell
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Trying digits 1-9 in each empty cell and undoing placements that break row, column, or box rules

problem_statement: Given a 9x9 Sudoku board where '.' marks an empty cell and '1'-'9' marks a clue, solve the puzzle. Every row, column, and 3x3 box must contain digits 1-9 exactly once. The input board has exactly one solution.
task: Print the solved 9x9 board as 9 lines of 9 digits with no spaces.
output_format: Print 9 lines each containing 9 digits of the solved board.

examples.explanation: Each empty cell is filled so every row, column, and 3x3 box holds 1-9 exactly once.

expected_algorithm.name: Constraint Checking
expected_algorithm.reason: Digits are placed only when no row, column, or box conflict exists, and wrong guesses are undone by backtracking.

complexity.time: O(9^E) worst case where E is empty cells, heavily pruned by constraints

hint: Find the next empty cell and try digits 1-9.
Accept a digit only when its row, column, and 3x3 box are conflict-free.
Undo the digit after the recursive call returns.
real_world_takeaway: Backtracking plus constraint checks is how Sudoku and other rule-based puzzles are solved completely.
